Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front, details below.

- Transient cross-region hops: our standard operational window for transient processing is up to 48 hours in the rare case of failover or cache rehydration. We treat anything longer than 48 hours as an incident and escalate to the customer with an approval path.

- Subprocessor roster: attaching the current roster and a certification statement enumerating which subprocessors may process APAC customer data and their principal jurisdiction.

I've attached:
- MedTel_DPA_Draft_v2.pdf (redline with the 48h language in Section 4.3)
- subprocessor_roster_2028-07.xlsx (includes host country and whether they handle persisted telemetry)

Next steps I suggest: Procurement can accept the roster + certification as evidence; Legal can request an addendum if they need a shorter window.

I'll note that our transient processing is usually limited to: cache rehydration, short-term replica synchronization, and disaster-recovery failover. We do not use those windows for analytics or model training.

On the roster: the few subprocessors headquartered outside APAC are limited to CDN providers and a monitoring vendor — we highlight those rows in the spreadsheet.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Security & Privacy Program Manager, Redwood Inference
